title: Translation groupoid on the universal finite source parts
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ a groupoid scheme over $S$ [def-a1-groupoid-scheme], with $s,t$ separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] and locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose an $S$-scheme $M$ represents the following functor: on an $S$-scheme $T$ its elements are pairs $(a,Z)$, where $a:T\to U$ and $Z\subseteq R\times_{s,U,a}T$ is an open subscheme finite over $T$ containing the section $(ea,\mathrm{id}_T)$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Assume the forgetful morphism $g:M\to U$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and denote its universal open subscheme by $Q\subseteq R\times_{s,U,g}M$. Then $Q$ and $M$ carry a groupoid scheme structure over $S$, with a morphism of groupoids $(M,Q)\to(U,R)$ whose object map is $g$ and arrow map $Q\to R$ is the universal projection. On test schemes a point of $Q$ is a triple $(a,Z,z)$ with $z:T\to R$, $sz=a$ and $(z,\mathrm{id}_T)$ factoring through $Z$. The structure maps are
$$s_Q(a,Z,z)=(a,Z),\qquad t_Q(a,Z,z)=(tz,c(Z,iz)),$$
$$e_Q(a,Z)=(a,Z,ea),\qquad i_Q(a,Z,z)=(tz,c(Z,iz),iz),$$
and
$$c_Q\big((a_1,Z_1,z_1),(a_2,Z_2,z_2)\big)=(a_2,Z_2,c(z_1,z_2))$$
for composable triples. Here $c(Z,iz)$ is the image of $Z$ under the isomorphism $r\mapsto c(r,iz)$ between the two source fibres, with inverse $r\mapsto c(r,z)$. These formulas define morphisms and satisfy all groupoid axioms. Both $s_Q,t_Q:Q\to M$ are finite; $Q\subseteq R\times_UM$ is open and closed. No affineness or quasi-finiteness of $U,R$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 04RU (lemma-finite-part-groupoid), together with the explicit structure maps in Section section-finite-part-groupoid. Finiteness of target follows from source finiteness and the inverse involution.

proof.text: For an $S$-scheme $T$ put $R_a=R\times_{s,U,a}T$. By the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product], a map $T\to Q$ is exactly $(a,Z,z)$ as in the statement: its map to $M$ classifies $(a,Z)$, and its map to $R$ is $z$, with the pair factoring through the universal open. Write $rz=c(r,z)$, and define $\tau_z:R_a\to R_{tz}$ by $r\mapsto rz^{-1}$. This is a morphism of $T$-schemes, using $c,i$ and the fibre-product property. Its inverse is $r\mapsto rz$, since $(rz^{-1})z=r$ and $(rz)z^{-1}=r$ by [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. These equations hold on every test scheme over $T$, including nonreduced ones, so are equalities of morphisms by [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful].

source.place: Tag 04RU (lemma-finite-part-groupoid), preceding explicit construction in section-finite-part-groupoid; verification omitted there and supplied here.

proof.text: The image $Z'=\tau_z(Z)$ is an open subscheme of $R_{tz}$ by [def-weil-open-immersion]. The restriction $Z\to Z'$ is an isomorphism over $T$; hence $Z'\to T$ is finite, directly from [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] on affine opens. Moreover $\tau_z(z)=e(tz)$ and $\tau_z(e(a))=z^{-1}$. Thus $Z'$ contains both the unit at $tz$ and the section $z^{-1}$, proving that the proposed target and inverse have values in $M(T)$ and $Q(T)$. The source and unit formulas are well defined because $Z$ contains $e(a)$. For a base change $T'\to T$, openness and finiteness persist by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a); the pulled-back translation has the same two components $c(-,i(z|_{T'}))$ and the projection to $T'$. Uniqueness in [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies it with $\tau_{z|_{T'}}$. Therefore pulling back $Z'$ gives the translated pullback of $Z$, and all four rules commute with base change.

source.place: Tag 04RU (lemma-finite-part-groupoid), preceding explicit construction in section-finite-part-groupoid; verification omitted there and supplied here.

proof.text: For composable triples $q_j=(a_j,Z_j,z_j)$ the equality $s_Q(q_1)=t_Q(q_2)$ says $a_1=tz_2$ and $Z_1=\tau_{z_2}(Z_2)$. Since $z_1$ factors through $Z_1$, its inverse image under $\tau_{z_2}$, namely $z_1z_2$, factors through $Z_2$ as a section of schemes. Also $s(z_1z_2)=a_2$ by [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. Hence the displayed composition formula is well defined. It commutes with base change because $c$ does and the second triple's pair pulls back to its classifying pair. The domain of composable pairs is the fibre product $Q\times_{s_Q,M,t_Q}Q$ by [def-pc-fibre-product]. Apply [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] in the category of $S$-schemes to the natural rules of steps 1–3: they give actual $S$-morphisms $s_Q,t_Q,e_Q,i_Q,c_Q$.

source.place: Tag 04RU (lemma-finite-part-groupoid), preceding explicit construction in section-finite-part-groupoid; verification omitted there and supplied here.

proof.text: For composable $z_1,z_2$, associativity and inversion in [def-a1-groupoid-scheme] give $\tau_{z_1z_2}(r)=r(z_1z_2)^{-1}=(rz_2^{-1})z_1^{-1}$, so $\tau_{z_1z_2}=\tau_{z_1}\tau_{z_2}$. This is an identity of $T$-scheme isomorphisms by [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful]; thus it also identifies their images of open subschemes. Consequently the composite triple has source $(a_2,Z_2)$ and target $(tz_1,\tau_{z_1}(Z_1))$, exactly the source of $q_2$ and target of $q_1$. The formulas also give $s_Qe_Q=t_Qe_Q=1_M$ and $s_Qi_Q=t_Q$, $t_Qi_Q=s_Q$, using $\tau_{e(a)}=1$ and $\tau_{z^{-1}}\tau_z=1$.

source.place: Tag 04RU (lemma-finite-part-groupoid), preceding explicit construction in section-finite-part-groupoid; verification omitted there and supplied here.

proof.text: Both bracketings of three composable triples have the same source pair $(a_3,Z_3)$ and arrow $(z_1z_2)z_3=z_1(z_2z_3)$ by [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]; step 4 verifies their composability. The left unit at $t_Q(q)$ and right unit at $s_Q(q)$ both compose with $q=(a,Z,z)$ to give source pair $(a,Z)$ and arrow $e(tz)z=z=ze(a)$. The composites $i_Q(q)q$ and $qi_Q(q)$ have source pairs $(a,Z)$ and $(tz,\tau_z Z)$ and arrows $z^{-1}z=e(a)$ and $zz^{-1}=e(tz)$, respectively. They are exactly the two required identity triples. Thus on every test $S$-scheme the operations form a groupoid, naturally in that scheme, which is the groupoid-scheme criterion of [def-a1-groupoid-scheme] with all maps over $S$. Equality of triples here is equality of pairs and actual scheme morphisms, not just geometric-point equality.

source.place: Tag 04RU (lemma-finite-part-groupoid), preceding explicit construction in section-finite-part-groupoid; verification omitted there and supplied here.

proof.text: The maps $(g,Q\to R)$ preserve source and target since the source and target of the arrow coordinate $z$ are $a$ and $tz$. They preserve the identity, inverse and composition since their arrow coordinates are exactly $e(a)$, $i(z)$ and $c(z_1,z_2)$. These equalities, checked on arbitrary test schemes, are equalities of morphisms by [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful]. This proves the asserted morphism of groupoids. Applying the inverse formula twice gives $(a,\tau_{z^{-1}}\tau_z Z,z)=(a,Z,z)$ by step 4, so $i_Q^2=1_Q$. Thus $i_Q$ is an isomorphism and $t_Q=s_Q\circ i_Q$.

source.place: Tag 04RU (lemma-finite-part-groupoid), preceding explicit construction in section-finite-part-groupoid; verification omitted there and supplied here.

proof.text: The source $s_Q:Q\to M$ is the universal finite family, so is finite by hypothesis. Since $i_Q$ is an isomorphism, $t_Q=s_Q\circ i_Q$ is finite too: on an affine open of $M$ its inverse image is isomorphic over that open to the corresponding inverse image for $s_Q$, hence has the same finite coordinate algebra [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. No affineness of $R$ or $U$ enters this affine-local check.

source.place: Tag 04RU (lemma-finite-part-groupoid), preceding explicit construction in section-finite-part-groupoid; verification omitted there and supplied here.

proof.text: Set $X=R\times_{s,U,g}M$ and let $j:Q\hookrightarrow X$ be the universal open. The morphism $X\to M$ is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-base-change], since $s$ is separated. The finite $Q\to M$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]. Apply [lemma-nagata-proper-to-separated-target] to $Q\xrightarrow{j}X\to M$: $j$ is proper. In particular its image is closed by the definition of universally closed in [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Since $j$ already identifies $Q$ with an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion], this proves that $Q$ is open and closed in $X$. This uses no flatness or quasi-finiteness of $s,t$.
